title: What an Optional Supplemental Benefit Rider Pays on a Claim Line
content:
Standing basis of the claims desk for a dental, vision or hearing line claimed under any of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders.

## 1. The share and the base it is taken on

The rider pays the share of the allowed amount its benefit category fixes for the tier held, always worked out from the allowed amount and never from what the provider charged. The share taken is the coinsurance percentage or flat allowance the per-tier terms give for this line's benefit category.

## 2. The rider must be active on the date of service

The rider stands at active on the date of service of the line. This is read before the line is settled, from the rider's own record — its reference, its standing and the day from which its benefits became payable — and from that record alone.

## 3. The deductible

Any deductible the tier carries is met first, out of the categories the tier takes it on, before any coinsurance applies; preventive care is never subject to a deductible on any tier.

## 4. Flat allowances on vision and hearing

Vision and hearing benefits are paid as flat allowances rather than percentages: the rider pays up to the frame, lens, contact lens or hearing aid allowance and the member pays the rest, and an unused part of an allowance is never paid out in cash.

## 5. The benefit year maximum, no longer in force

The clause "The rider pays nothing more once the benefit year's annual maximum is reached, and a line that would cross it is paid only up to what is left; the member is told the remaining figure whenever they ask about treatment" is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which what is left of the benefit year's maximum is worked out.

## 6. Balance billing

A network provider may not bill the member above the allowed amount on the tiers that carry balance billing protection, and a member shown such a bill is told it is wrong and the provider is contacted.

## 7. Out-of-network lines, no longer in force

The clause "An out-of-network line is paid at the tier's out-of-network share of the allowed amount, and where that share is zero the line is denied and the member is told which network providers are near them" is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which the amount the benefit is taken from is settled where the provider is outside the network.

## 8. Predetermination

Where the treatment plan value is above the tier's predetermination threshold, an approved predetermination covering that service and still inside its validity period is on record. This is settled before the line is processed, on the plan's own records: the claim line's reference, the predetermination it names and its allowed amount, alongside the rider service request carrying the predetermination, the answer given on it and the day that answer was given.

## 9. Late filing

A claim reaching the plan more than the tier's filing window after the date of service is denied on the ground that it was filed after the window closed, and the denial is explained to the member rather than simply recorded.
